result: In 140 PASC patients at a post-COVID clinic, 43% met IOM 2015 ME/CFS criteria; PEM was reported by 82.8%.
reason: already cited: preprint of Bonilla 2023 (Front Neurol), same title and cohort

result: In the expanded Dubbo cohort (n=484), 90 (19%) met CFS criteria at 6 months; severity of the acute illness and concurrent mood disturbance predicted prolonged illness and PIFS, and NPY haplotypes were examined as predictors.
reason: same DIOS cohort as Hickie 2006, so not independent; adds a larger sample, mood and NPY genetics

result: In 409 Norwegian cases vs 810 controls and 2,105 UK Biobank cases vs 4,786 controls, the two previously reported TRA-locus SNPs (rs11157573, rs17255510) did not associate with ME/CFS and no TRA SNP survived multiple-testing correction.
reason: null replication supports the finding's claim that candidate signals do not replicate; it is not a contradiction

result: Among 200 PCR-confirmed post-COVID patients tested 45-120 days after infection, those with post-COVID syndrome had lower peak VO2 (25.8 vs 28.8 ml/kg/min, p=0.017), were less likely to reach the anaerobic threshold and had more symptoms during CPET, robust to adjustment.
reason: independent cohort, same measure, same direction

result: In 29 non-hospitalized post-COVID patients with severe self-reported motor and cognitive fatigue (FSMC), only 2 showed treadmill walking performance fatigability (FKS >4), and oxygen uptake and ventilation were in the normal range; there was no control group.
reason: treadmill gait fatigability in long COVID, not the grip fMRI/brain-activation measure in ME/CFS; no atlas finding covers this measure

result: Among 279 long COVID patients at an Okayama aftercare clinic, 16.8% had physician-diagnosed ME/CFS (Fukuda, CCC and IOM), with an equal sex ratio and more severe acute COVID-19 in those with ME/CFS.
reason: clinic-based post-COVID ME/CFS rate with physician-applied criteria and acute-severity association; adds to the clinic-cohort evidence in the finding

result: The 10-min NASA lean test worsened symptoms and produced hemodynamic and smartphone-measured cognitive abnormalities in long COVID (n=42) and ME/CFS (n=26) but not in 20 healthy controls, with follow-up to 7 days.
reason: same test; adds a long COVID group, cognitive measures and post-test time course

result: In a population-based Zurich cohort (1,543 infected, 628 uninfected), 25% had not recovered by 6 months, and of those 67% and 58% were still not recovered at 12 and 18 months; excess symptom risk vs uninfected was 17% at 6 months and 20% at 12 months, highest for taste/smell, PEM, fatigue and concentration.
reason: population-based natural course of post-COVID non-recovery with uninfected controls; does not apply ME/CFS criteria, so not a replication

result: A meta-analysis of 39 CPET studies (2,209 people) found peak VO2 7.4 ml/kg/min lower in infected vs uninfected and 4.9 ml/kg/min (95% CI 3.4-6.4) lower in long COVID vs those without symptoms.
reason: already cited: preprint of Durstenfeld 2022 (JAMA Netw Open)

result: Antibody levels to 122 pathogen antigens in ME/CFS vs age-, sex- and BMI-matched controls did not implicate any single pathogen, but showed sex-based differences in humoral immunity; the abstract gives no sample size.
reason: null serology result supports the finding; 'extends' overstates it, and only the sex-difference aspect is new
